narrative:
The model predicts you have a 22% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to strengthen your performance before the exams.

The prediction is driven mainly by three aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. While this might sound positive, students who have never failed tend to receive slightly lower final grades in this dataset, possibly because the model sees a lack of prior academic struggle as an indicator that you may not have developed the resilience or study habits needed for the final push. This feature pushed the prediction toward failing.

The second strongest influence is that you are receiving extra educational support at school. Most students who passed did not need this support, so the model interprets it as a sign that you are already struggling and require help, further increasing the chance of failing.

Third, you have expressed a strong desire to pursue higher education. This is actually a positive factor that pulls the prediction back toward passing, as every student who passed also wanted to continue studying. However, this encouraging signal was not strong enough to outweigh the first two factors.

To improve, focus on building consistent study routines, make full use of the support you already receive, and reduce your high weekend alcohol consumption, which stands out compared with most successful students. Taking the remedial courses seriously will help turn this prediction around. (248 words)
